data.title: Zymeworks Announces Participation in Upcoming Investor Conferences
data.description:
VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Zymeworks Inc. (Nasdaq: ZYME), a biotechnology company managing a portfolio of licensed healthcare assets while developing a diverse pipeline of novel, multifunctional biotherapeutics, today announced will participate in the following upcoming investor conferences:

  • Evercore Healthcare Conference: Management will participate in one-on-one meetings and a fireside chat on November 30 at 2:10 pm Eastern Time (ET) in Miami, FL
  • Citi’s 2026 Global Healthcare Conference: Management will participate in one-on-one meetings and a fireside chat on December 1 at 3:40 pm ET in Miami, FL

A live webcast of certain fireside chats will be available in the Investors section of the Zymeworks website at www.zymeworks.com, and a replay will be available following the events.

About Zymeworks Inc.

Zymeworks is a global biotechnology company building a diversified portfolio of healthcare assets designed to generate durable cash flows while advancing innovative medicines for difficult-to-treat diseases. The Company’s asset and royalty aggregation strategy combines a growing portfolio of commercial and near-commercial assets, including YUPELRI® (revefenacin), with a differentiated internal research and development engine. Zymeworks’ portfolio also includes Ziihera® (zanidatamab-hrii), a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody discovered and developed by Zymeworks and commercialized through global partnerships with Jazz Pharmaceuticals and BeOne Medicines, and pasritamig, a clinical-stage multispecific antibody developed by Johnson & Johnson using Zymeworks’ proprietary antibody engineering technologies.

Zymeworks is advancing a diverse pipeline of novel biotherapeutics, leveraging its proprietary Azymetric™ platform and expertise in antibody-drug conjugates, multispecific antibodies and other next-generation antibody technologies. These capabilities, together with Zymeworks’ integrated drug development expertise, enable the Company to develop differentiated therapeutics and create value through both internal innovation and strategic partnerships.

For more information about Zymeworks, its portfolio and pipeline, visit www.zymeworks.com and follow @ZymeworksInc on X.

data.title: First Atlantic Nickel & Cobalt Attends Critical Minerals Briefing on Capitol Hill, Highlighting New Cerium Refining Technology That Extracted 98% of the Nickel and 82% of the Cobalt From Pipestone XL Awaruite (Ni-Fe-Co Alloy) in 20 Minutes Without Smelting, in Columbia University Research Funded by the U.S. Department of Energy's ARPA-E MINER Program
data.description:
GRAND FALLS-WINDSOR, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- First Atlantic Nickel & Cobalt Corp. (TSXV: FAN) (OTCQB: FANCF) (FSE: P210) ("First Atlantic" or the "Company") is pleased to announce its attendance at the Fastmarkets Critical Minerals and Materials Briefing, taking place today, November 19, 2026, on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC.1 The Company is attending to highlight the new cerium refining technology developed at Columbia University. As reported on November 18, 2026,2 the technology extracted 98% of the nickel and 82% of the cobalt in 20 minutes from awaruite (Ni-Fe-Co alloy) concentrate sourced from the Company's Pipestone XL Nickel-Cobalt Alloy Project, with approximately 90% of the nickel extracted within the first 5 minutes. The process operated at room temperature, with no smelting and no sulfuric acid pretreatment, as reported on November 18, 2026.3

First Atlantic has also launched a new website at www.fanickel.com, featuring an interactive chart of the cerium refining results, drill results and interactive maps of the Pipestone XL Project.

The briefing is being held on Capitol Hill4, and brings together federal policymakers, critical minerals producers and processors, defense and aerospace leaders, investors and industrial buyers to examine the next phase of U.S. critical minerals strategy, including domestic mining, processing and refining capacity. The program includes a fireside chat, "What's Next for Critical Minerals? U.S. Policy Priorities," with U.S. Representatives Gary Palmer and Paul Tonko, Chairman and Ranking Member respectively, of the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Environment. First Atlantic Chief Executive Officer Adrian Smith and Strategic Advisor Dr. Douglas Wicks, former Program Director of the U.S. Department of Energy's ARPA-E MINER program and Geologic Hydrogen portfolio, are attending on behalf of the Company.

Gary Stanley, Strategic Advisor to First Atlantic and former Director of the Office of Critical Minerals and Metals at the U.S. Department of Commerce, is a panelist on "Critical Minerals and U.S. Defense Readiness: Securing Strategic Supply Chains" alongside Jeffrey Frankston, Deputy Assistant Secretary of War for Industrial Base Resilience at the U.S. Department of War.5 First Atlantic welcomes the opportunity to meet with government, defense and industry representatives during the briefing.

First Atlantic is working with Columbia University, its Research Partner, to advance the new breakthrough cerium refining technology developed at Columbia University as a domestic refining option for awaruite (Ni-Fe-Co alloy), a naturally occurring magnetic nickel-iron-cobalt alloy that is concentrated by magnetic separation and flotation without smelting.6 The Columbia University research was funded by the U.S. Department of Energy's ARPA-E MINER program, which was created to increase domestic production of critical minerals such as nickel and cobalt. Nickel sulfide concentrates, by contrast, must be smelted before they can be refined, and only two pyrometallurgical nickel smelters remain in operation in North America, both in Sudbury, Ontario, while the only nickel smelter in the United States, in Riddle, Oregon, closed permanently in 1998.7 Because awaruite does not need a smelter, the Columbia University research indicates strong potential for First Atlantic to develop a vertically integrated, onshore nickel and cobalt supply chain in North America: mining and concentrating awaruite at Pipestone XL in Newfoundland, then shipping a high-grade nickel-cobalt alloy concentrate directly into downstream refining to produce Class 1 nickel metal or nickel sulfate (NiSO₄), without a smelting step.

First Atlantic welcomes direct calls from shareholders and prospective investors. Rob Guzman, Investor Relations, is available at +1-844-592-6337 or by email at rob@fanickel.com to answer questions about this news release or the Company. Because call volume is high, please leave a voice message or email Rob to request a call back.

KEY HIGHLIGHTS

  • Capitol Hill briefing on U.S. critical minerals strategy: First Atlantic is attending the Fastmarkets Critical Minerals and Materials Briefing 2026 in Washington, DC, where Strategic Advisor Gary Stanley is a panelist on "Critical Minerals and U.S. Defense Readiness: Securing Strategic Supply Chains."
  • New cerium refining technology: Columbia University research funded by the U.S. Department of Energy’s ARPA-E MINER program extracted 98% of the nickel and 82% of the cobalt from Pipestone XL awaruite concentrate in 20 minutes, with approximately 90% of the nickel extracted in the first 5 minutes (see Figure 2).
  • Cerium is recycled and reused in the refining loop: The cerium solution works at room temperature and atmospheric pressure, with no sulfuric acid pretreatment. Spent cerium(III) is converted back to cerium(IV) by electrochemical regeneration and reused in the leach in a closed-loop process design (see Figure 3).
  • Awaruite nickel-cobalt alloy outperformed nickel sulfide: Compared with nickel sulfide samples from Tamarack, awaruite yielded up to 66% more nickel extraction in one-third of the time, while the sulfide samples consumed up to 16 times more cerium (see Table 1).
  • High-grade magnetic alloy concentrate with no smelting required: The Company's ONSHORE MAX™ process produced a magnetic alloy concentrate averaging 67.4% nickel, grading up to 71.9% nickel and 1.76% cobalt, compared with 10% to 15% nickel in typical sulfide concentrates.
  • Vertically integrated North American supply chain: Mining and concentrating awaruite in Newfoundland, then refining the alloy concentrate in the United States with cerium refining technology, has the potential to keep nickel and cobalt in North America from mine to refined metal.
  • U.S. government engagement: First Atlantic is a member of the Defense Industrial Base Consortium (DIBC) and has applied under RPP-CM-26-01, "Domestic Processing Capabilities of Critical Minerals," with Columbia University as its Research Partner.
  • New website launched: First Atlantic has launched a new website at www.fanickel.com, featuring an interactive chart of the cerium refining results, drill results and interactive maps of the Pipestone XL Project.

Dr. Douglas Wicks, Strategic Advisor to First Atlantic and former Program Director of the U.S. Department of Energy's ARPA-E MINER program and Geologic Hydrogen portfolio, commented:

"The ARPA-E MINER program was created to develop commercially scalable technologies that increase domestic production of critical minerals such as nickel and cobalt. As its Program Director I funded this Columbia University research, and the results on First Atlantic's awaruite concentrate from Pipestone XL demonstrate the successful test of cerium refining: approximately 98% of the nickel and 82% of the cobalt extracted in 20 minutes, at room temperature, without smelting or sulfuric acid. Because the cerium is regenerated with electricity and reused, the process has the potential to be cost-effective and scalable to commercial production, and to help onshore the refining of Class 1 nickel metal or battery-grade nickel in North America."

Source: graphical abstract, Donovan et al. (2026), ACS Sustainable Resource Management.

NEW CERIUM REFINING TECHNOLOGY: REFINING AWARUITE WITHOUT A SMELTER, AT ROOM TEMPERATURE, WITH NO SULFURIC ACID PRETREATMENT

In Columbia University's new cerium refining technology, the nickel is dissolved (leached) by a cerium salt solution at room temperature and atmospheric pressure, with no heating and no pressure vessel. Two cerium(IV) salts were tested, and both extracted approximately 98% of the nickel from Pipestone XL awaruite concentrate in 20 minutes (97.5% and 98.1%), with no acid pretreatment. That is up to 66% more nickel, extracted in one-third of the time, compared with the Tamarack nickel sulfide samples.

In the study, awaruite achieved higher nickel extraction in less time, with less cerium consumption, than the Tamarack nickel sulfide samples. Under the same conditions, the sulfide samples reached 59% to 82.5% nickel extraction after 60 minutes, and consumed up to 16 times more cerium than awaruite (sample CGO-HM, Table 1). The best sulfide result, 84% (sample SMSU-HM, acid pretreated), was reached only after the sample was first treated with hot sulfuric acid to remove iron sulfide (pyrrhotite); without that pretreatment, the same material reached 70.5% (sample SMSU-HM, no pretreatment).9 Awaruite contains no sulfur, which is why it leaches quickly, consumes little cerium and needs no acid pretreatment.

The cerium is not used up in the process. It works in a closed loop: cerium(IV), the active form, dissolves the nickel and cobalt and is converted to cerium(III), the spent form. An electrochemical cell then uses electricity to convert the cerium(III) back to cerium(IV), which is returned to the leach and reused. Columbia demonstrated multiple cerium regeneration cycles, so the cerium acts as a recyclable carrier and not as a reagent that is consumed.


Figure 2: Nickel extraction over time with the new cerium refining technology. Pipestone XL awaruite concentrate reached approximately 90% nickel extraction in 5 minutes and 98% in 20 minutes, compared with 59% to 82.5% after 60 minutes for the Tamarack nickel sulfide samples in the same Columbia University study. Data from Donovan et al. (2026), ACS Sustainable Resource Management; points between the start and end values are approximate, read from the paper's charts. Chart by First Atlantic.


Figure 3: The cerium closed loop. Cerium(IV) dissolves the nickel and cobalt and is converted to cerium(III); electricity converts the cerium(III) back to cerium(IV), which is reused, at room temperature and atmospheric pressure with no smelter. Diagram by First Atlantic.


Figure 4: First Atlantic Chief Executive Officer Adrian Smith (left) and Strategic Advisor Gary Stanley (right), former Director of the Office of Critical Minerals and Metals at the U.S. Department of Commerce, at the Columbia Electrochemical Energy Center laboratory, Department of Chemical Engineering, Columbia University, in New York, standing in front of the cerium leach solutions and nickel products from Columbia's cerium leaching testwork.

CERIUM: AN ABUNDANT, LOW-COST RARE EARTH PRODUCED BY MP MATERIALS AT MOUNTAIN PASS, CALIFORNIA

Cerium is the most abundant of the rare earth elements, more common in the Earth's crust than copper. It is also one of the cheapest: cerium oxide averaged US$1.71 per kilogram in 2025, according to the U.S. Geological Survey.10 Cerium is produced alongside the magnet rare earths and is in surplus, with one industry estimate placing 2024 output near 167,000 tonnes against demand near 60,000 tonnes, and it is not on China's export control lists.11 In the United States, MP Materials produces cerium chloride as one of four rare earth compounds at Mountain Pass, California,12 which the company describes as the only integrated rare earth site of its kind in the Western Hemisphere.13 In Columbia's process, the cerium is designed to be regenerated with electricity after it dissolves the nickel and returned to the leach for reuse.

THE MIDSTREAM BOTTLENECK: SMELTING CAPACITY AND SULFURIC ACID SUPPLY

Inco's Thompson smelter complex in Manitoba began production in 1961.14 Vale closed the Thompson smelter and refinery on July 31, 2018,15 having been advised that compliance with federal sulphur dioxide regulations would cost approximately $1 billion.16 The only nickel smelter in the United States, at Riddle, Oregon, closed permanently in 1998.17 Only two pyrometallurgical nickel smelters remain in operation in North America, both located in Sudbury, Ontario.18

Conventional nickel refining depends heavily on sulfuric acid, and that dependence was exposed in 2026. The Middle East supplies approximately 25% of the world's sulfur, and 45% to 50% of seaborne sulfur trade moves through the Strait of Hormuz.19 Following the outbreak of conflict in the region on February 28, 2026, the price of sulfur delivered to Indonesia rose from approximately US$563 per tonne to a peak near US$1,300 per tonne,20 and on April 10, 2026 China announced a near-total ban on sulfuric acid exports.21 On March 13, 2026, an article published by the Modern War Institute at West Point warned that the sulfur shortage threatens nickel, cobalt and copper processing and recommended that the U.S. Department of War fund research into non-sulfuric leaching.22

PIPESTONE XL: FIVE AWARUITE ZONES ON A 30-KILOMETER TREND AND A SMELTER-FREE ROUTE TO DOWNSTREAM PROCESSING IN NORTH AMERICA

Pipestone XL is First Atlantic's wholly owned project covering the entire 30-kilometer Pipestone Ophiolite Complex in central Newfoundland. Five zones of awaruite mineralization have been identified along the trend: RPM, Alloy Max, Super Gulp, Atlantic Lake and Chrome Pond. RPM is the most advanced, with drilling outlining magnetically recoverable awaruite over more than 1.2 kilometers of strike and more than 800 meters of width. The Alloy Max target area is approximately 4 kilometers long and up to 1.5 kilometers wide, and every hole assayed there has returned magnetically recoverable nickel.

Awaruite (Ni₃Fe) is a naturally occurring, magnetic nickel-iron-cobalt alloy that contains no sulphur. Electron microprobe analysis of awaruite from the RPM Zone averaged 77.62% nickel and 1.69% cobalt.23 Because the nickel is already in metallic form, it can be concentrated by magnetic separation and flotation without smelting, roasting or high-pressure acid leaching. In initial test work using the Company's ONSHORE MAX™ (Magnetic Alloy eXtraction) process, magnetic separation produced a concentrate grading approximately 1.6% nickel, which flotation upgraded to an alloy concentrate averaging 67.4% nickel and grading up to 71.9% nickel and 1.76% cobalt.24 A typical nickel concentrate grades 10% to 15% nickel, according to the Nickel Institute.25

Figure 5: The Pipestone XL Nickel-Cobalt (Ni-Fe-Co) Alloy Project. Top: 3D view of the 30-kilometer Pipestone XL trend with the Company's magnetic survey draped on terrain, showing the RPM, Alloy Max, Super Gulp, Atlantic Lake and Chrome Pond Zones. Bottom, left to right: bedrock sample (two views) with visible disseminated awaruite, from beneath shallow overburden at an Alloy Max drill pad (April 8, 2026 news release); drill core with visible awaruite, hole XL-26-18 at 32 meters, Alloy Max South (October 13, 2026); photomicrograph of an awaruite grain up to approximately 2,000 microns, hole AN-25-08 at 370 meters, RPM Zone (September 25, 2025). Awaruite grades of 77.62% nickel and 1.69% cobalt are the RPM Zone electron microprobe average (May 21, 2026); the 67.4% nickel concentrate grade is the average of four flotation tests (June 24, 2026).

A magnetic nickel-cobalt (Ni-Fe-Co) alloy concentrate from the Pipestone XL Project has the potential to be a large-scale source of nickel and cobalt for North America. Because the concentrate does not need a smelter, it can bypass the midstream smelting bottleneck and move directly from the mine to battery chemical refining or to stainless steel and specialty alloy production, keeping the supply chain onshore. Pipestone XL has year-round road access, nearby high-voltage transmission and hydroelectric power from the Bay d'Espoir generating station, and is approximately 200 kilometers from Vale's Long Harbour nickel processing plant and Gander International Airport. The Company is also evaluating chromium as a potential co-product and low-carbon Engineered Mineral Hydrogen with VEMA Hydrogen.


Figure 6: The ONSHORE MAX™ (Magnetic Alloy eXtraction) process. Top, left to right, bench-scale test work at SGS Canada Inc. on RPM Zone material: drum separator producing a magnetic concentrate of approximately 1.6% nickel by low-intensity magnetic separation; rougher flotation cell; awaruite alloy concentrate under a magnet. Four flotation tests averaged 67.4% nickel (63.7% to 71.9%), with 1.76% cobalt in the final test (June 24, 2026 news release). Bottom: conceptual mine-to-refinery supply chain for awaruite alloy concentrate with no smelting step.

ABOUT FIRST ATLANTIC NICKEL & COBALT CORP.

First Atlantic Nickel & Cobalt Corp. (TSXV: FAN | OTCQB: FANCF | FSE: P210) is a critical mineral exploration company in Newfoundland and Labrador advancing the wholly owned Pipestone XL Nickel-Cobalt Alloy Project. The project spans the entire 30-kilometer Pipestone Ophiolite Complex, where five zones, RPM, Alloy Max, Super Gulp, Atlantic Lake and Chrome Pond, contain awaruite (Ni₃Fe), a naturally occurring magnetic nickel-iron-cobalt alloy averaging 77.62% nickel and 1.69% cobalt, with no sulphur and no sulphides. Drilling has outlined two large-scale zones of magnetically recoverable nickel at RPM and Alloy Max.

Because awaruite is already a magnetic metal alloy, it can be concentrated by magnetic separation and flotation without smelting, roasting or high-pressure acid leaching. The Company's ONSHORE MAX™ process has produced an alloy concentrate averaging 67.4% nickel and grading up to 71.9% nickel and 1.76% cobalt, and peer-reviewed Columbia University research has extracted 98% of the nickel and 82% of the cobalt from that concentrate in 20 minutes using a new cerium refining technology. The U.S. Geological Survey noted in 2012 that awaruite is much easier to concentrate than pentlandite, the principal sulphide of nickel.

Pipestone XL has year-round road access, nearby high-voltage transmission and hydroelectric power. First Atlantic has signed a letter of intent with VEMA Hydrogen for a proposed joint venture to develop low-carbon Engineered Mineral Hydrogen at Pipestone XL, and is evaluating chromium as a potential co-product. The Company also holds the Ophiolite-X and North Arm projects in western Newfoundland, and is a member of the U.S. Defense Industrial Base Consortium. Newfoundland and Labrador has ranked among the top 10 jurisdictions worldwide for investment attractiveness or mining policy in every Fraser Institute Annual Survey of Mining Companies since 2022.

QUALIFIED PERSON

Adrian Smith, P.Geo., a director and the Chief Executive Officer of the Company, is a qualified person as defined by NI 43-101. The qualified person is a member in good standing of the Professional Engineers and Geoscientists Newfoundland and Labrador (PEGNL) and is a registered professional geoscientist (P.Geo.). Mr. Smith has reviewed and approved the technical information disclosed herein. Mr. Smith has not independently verified the leaching results reported by Columbia University or the third-party information on the Tamarack Project, which are taken from the published sources cited. His verification of the scientific and technical information in this news release consisted of the review of the published paper and of the Company's records of the samples supplied to Columbia University.

DISCLOSURE

The leaching results in this news release are taken from a peer-reviewed paper by researchers at Columbia University, who are independent of the Company. The tests were batch tests at laboratory scale. Continuous operation, repeated regeneration of cerium on awaruite leach solutions, cerium losses and the recovery of nickel and cobalt from solution have not yet been demonstrated. The awaruite concentrate tested was produced in preliminary bench-scale test work at SGS Canada Inc. on a single composite sample from the RPM Zone and may not be representative of the mineralization as a whole. Information on the Tamarack project and on third-party smelters, sulfur markets and cerium markets is taken from the public sources cited and has not been independently verified by the Company.

Neither the TSX Venture Exchange nor its Regulation Services Provider (as that term is defined in policies of the TSX Venture Exchange) accepts responsibility for the adequacy or accuracy of this release.

FORWARD-LOOKING STATEMENTS

This news release contains “forward-looking information” within the meaning of applicable Canadian securities laws. Forward-looking information is generally identified by words such as “plans”, “expects”, “anticipates”, “intends”, “aims”, “objective”, “potential”, “designed to”, “will”, “may”, “could” and similar expressions, or statements that certain events or conditions “may” or “will” occur. Forward-looking information in this news release includes, but is not limited to, statements regarding the potential of cerium leaching as a processing route for awaruite concentrate from Pipestone XL; the potential for cerium to be regenerated electrochemically and reused in a closed loop; the potential for Pipestone XL to be a large-scale source of nickel and cobalt for North America; the potential for the Company to develop a vertically integrated North American nickel and cobalt supply chain, including by mining and concentrating awaruite in Newfoundland and refining the alloy concentrate in the United States; the potential for awaruite concentrate to bypass smelting and be processed into Class 1 nickel metal or nickel sulfate; the potential for cerium leaching to be cost-effective and to be scaled up to commercial production; the potential to process awaruite concentrate without smelting, roasting, high-pressure acid leaching or sulfuric acid pretreatment; continued collaboration with Columbia University; the Company’s application under RPP-CM-26-01 as a member of the Defense Industrial Base Consortium and the outcome of that application; the proposed joint venture with VEMA Hydrogen; the evaluation of chromium as a potential co-product; and the supply and pricing of sulfur, sulfuric acid, cerium and nickel.

Forward-looking information is based on a number of assumptions that management considers reasonable, including that the laboratory results reported by Columbia University are representative and can be reproduced; that further test work will proceed and that material for it will be available; that required permits and approvals will be received on a timely basis; that the Company’s current funds will be sufficient for its intended work; that collaboration with Columbia University will continue; that the Company will be able to obtain rights to use the cerium leaching process on acceptable terms; that cerium and electricity will be available at reasonable cost; that downstream refining capacity for awaruite concentrate can be developed or accessed in North America; that engagement with Indigenous groups and local communities will continue constructively; and that there will be no material adverse change in applicable laws or market conditions.

Forward-looking information is subject to known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors that may cause actual results, performance or achievements to differ materially from those expressed or implied. These include risks inherent in mineral exploration; the fact that the Company has not defined any mineral resources or mineral reserves at Pipestone XL; the fact that no economic study has been completed on Pipestone XL; the fact that the leaching results are from laboratory-scale batch tests and may not be reproduced in continuous operation or at a larger scale; the fact that the cerium process has not been demonstrated at pilot or commercial scale and that cerium regeneration, cerium losses and downstream recovery of nickel and cobalt remain to be demonstrated for awaruite; the fact that the cerium process was developed by Columbia University and the Company does not own or control it; the preliminary nature of the Company’s metallurgical test work and the fact that the ONSHORE MAX™ process has not been demonstrated at pilot or commercial scale; the absence of existing commercial-scale refining capacity for awaruite concentrate in North America and the capital required to develop it; changes in U.S. or Canadian trade policy, tariffs or cross-border regulation affecting the movement of concentrate between Canada and the United States; the fact that there is no assurance that the Company’s application under RPP-CM-26-01 will be selected or funded; failure to obtain, or delays in obtaining, permits or approvals; reliance on third-party information that the Company has not independently verified; volatility in nickel, cobalt, sulfur, sulfuric acid and cerium prices; the ability to obtain future financing on acceptable terms; dependence on key personnel; changes in laws, regulations and government policy; and general economic, market and business conditions. data.title: Alibaba Earnings Rebound Sharply as AI Profitability Improves
data.description:
By Tracy Qu

Alibaba Group recorded a surge in fiscal second-quarter profit as its AI profitability and e-commerce business improved.

The Hangzhou-based company has doubled down on artificial intelligence as a growth driver, a push that faces a new risk from heightened scrutiny about exports of chips to China. It has committed to spending more than $53 billion over three years to develop both the hardware and software that power AI.

Its success on that front holds the key to staying competitive amid challenges from other big tech firms and startups alike. But going all in on AI has proved a drag on profitability over recent quarters, putting pressure on Alibaba to deliver on its AI goals.

Its latest results look reassuring.

On Thursday, Alibaba said net profit tripled from a year earlier to 64.535 billion yuan, equivalent to $9.68 billion, for the three months ended September. Analysts polled by FactSet had expected 23.72 billion yuan. Revenue grew about 10% to 271.52 billion yuan, also better than market estimates.

Alibaba attributed the sharp profit improvement to higher net investment income and income from operations.

The earnings beat comes as Alibaba prepares a Hong Kong listing for its chip unit, T-Head, that investors view as a major validation of its efforts to produce in-house semiconductors. The business could fetch a valuation of $85 billion, according to Nomura estimates.

data.title: Ecceamerica Brings European Excellence to Canada: Organic EVO Oil Takes Center Stage in Toronto
data.description:
Ecceamerica Brings European Excellence to Canada: Organic EVO Oil Takes Center Stage in Toronto

From November 12 to 25, 2026, tastings and promotional activities at selected restaurants and retail outlets in Toronto and Oakville will showcase European extra virgin olive oil and the value of organic certification.

The quality of extra virgin olive oil begins long before it reaches the table. Cultivation practices, harvesting and processing techniques all help shape its aromas, intensity and flavor. Italy’s olive-growing biodiversity is particularly rich, with 743 olive varieties listed in the National Register of Fruit Tree Varieties, reflecting a longstanding connection between the land, agricultural traditions and quality production.

Organic certification adds another important dimension. It confirms compliance with European standards for organic production and processing, supports environmentally conscious production methods and helps consumers recognize products that meet specific requirements.

These values are central to Ecceamerica, a project promoted by Unaprol – the Italian Olive Consortium and CAP – Confederação dos Agricultores de Portugal, co-financed by the European Union under Regulation (EU) No. 1144/2014. The three-year program promotes European agri-food excellence in the United States and Canada, with a focus on organic extra virgin olive oil and organic wine. Through information and promotional activities, it aims to strengthen awareness and recognition of these products in both markets.

In Canada, from November 12 to 25, extra virgin olive oil will be featured in a series of tastings and promotional initiatives at selected restaurants and retail outlets in Toronto and Oakville. Visitors will have the opportunity to discover the product’s distinctive characteristics, explore its quality and learn more about the value of European organic production.

Specially trained personnel will guide the tastings and answer questions about extra virgin olive oil, including its characteristics and organic production methods. Dedicated informational materials will also be provided to help consumers better understand the product and make informed choices.

The activities are designed not only to offer a tasting experience, but also to create opportunities for direct dialogue about origin, production standards and everyday use.

By bringing European extra virgin olive oil directly to Canadian consumers, Ecceamerica seeks to highlight its quality, strengthen its recognition and encourage greater familiarity with organic certification.

Detailed schedules for participating restaurants and retail locations will be available on the project website.

For more information and updates, visit https://ecceamerica.eu/ and follow Ecceamerica on Facebook and Instagram.

data.title: LASE to Premiere Quantum Bullet(TM) at Counter UAS Technology Conference in Washington, D.C.
data.description:
ORLANDO, FL / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / LASE Corp. (NASDAQ:LASE), an emerging laser technology company developing laser and directed-energy solutions for the defense, pharmaceutical, semiconductor and industrial markets ("LASE" or the "Company"), today announced that it will premiere its Quantum Bullet™ anti-drone platform at Counter Unmanned Aircraft System ("UAS") Technology USA, taking place November 30 through December 2, 2026, in Washington, D.C., where Dmitri Nikitin, Executive Chairman of LASE Corp., will also present as a featured speaker.

This event brings together military, government and industry leaders to address the rapidly evolving threat posed by unmanned aerial systems and the technologies being developed to defeat them. This year's conference speakers include senior representatives of Joint Interagency Task Force 401 (JIATF-401), the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering, the U.S. Army, the Air Force Research Laboratory, U.S. Northern Command and the Department of Homeland Security. Last year's conference drew attendees from more than a dozen countries, NATO, and allied ministries of defense, as well as leading defense contractors.

This premiere complements the Company's previously announced introduction of Quantum Bullet™ at the Interservice/Industry Training, Simulation and Education Conference (I/ITSEC), taking place November 30 through December 3, 2026, in Orlando, Florida.

The Quantum Bullet™ product line includes the Company's Laser Shield Anti-Drone ("LSAD") Series, a modular directed-energy platform being developed to address Group 1 and Group 2 drone threats. LSAD is designed to combine proprietary laser-based counter-drone capabilities with multi-sensor detection, tracking, targeting and command-and-control ("C2") systems supplied by LASE and its integration partners, supporting either standalone deployment or integration into multilayered air-defense networks.

LASE is developing LSAD as a modular offering that can be configured with different laser and power capabilities for different tactical scenarios. Its Dazzler configuration is intended to disrupt the optical and LIDAR sensors of Group 1 and Group 2 drones, while higher-energy palletized and crawler configurations, the latter designed for rapid all-terrain deployment, are being developed for destructive engagement of drone threats. Development, integration, testing and customer evaluation remain necessary before commercialization.

Dmitri Nikitin, Executive Chairman of LASE Corp said, "What we have developed with Quantum Bullet™ is a fundamentally different approach to counter-drone defense. It is designed to deliver the precision, effectiveness and cost efficiency needed to address one of the military's most urgent and widespread threats: Group 1 and Group 2 drones. But what makes Quantum Bullet™ particularly compelling is its versatility. It is not simply a standalone weapon. It is a modular, mobile and integrated defense platform designed to operate independently or as part of a larger, layered defense system."

Dmitri Nikitin continued, "We believe the future of counter-drone defense will depend on technologies that work together, adapt to evolving threats and can be deployed wherever our military needs them. That is exactly what we are building with Quantum Bullet™.

Mr. Nikitin, the Company's founder, brings more than three decades of experience in laser technology innovation spanning marking, cutting, welding, cleaning, glass separation and semiconductor processing. He co-developed the world's first high-power fiber laser cutting system and developed a first-of-its-kind mobile fiber-laser platform for military mine-clearing applications. Mr. Nikitin holds an engineering degree in industrial electronics and quantum mechanics from Moscow Power Engineering University and a Ph.D. from the Ministry of Electronics Industry of the USSR, and he is a named inventor on three patent applications relating to Bulk-to-Shape technology.

Quantum Bullet™ is a registered trademark with the USPTO.

For more information on LASE Corp. and its brands, please visit www.lase.com.

LASE Corp. (NASDAQ:LASE), formerly Laser Photonics Corporation, is an emerging laser technology company developing laser and directed-energy solutions for the defense, pharmaceutical, semiconductor and industrial markets. Through internal development, strategic acquisitions and partnerships, LASE intends to expand its technology portfolio, strengthen its advanced manufacturing capabilities and scale the enterprise profitably.

PR Newswire

BEIJING, Nov. 19, 2026

BEIJING, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ROBOTERA, an AI-native embodied intelligence company, was invited to the 2026 APEC CEO Summit for the second consecutive year, becoming the only embodied intelligence company focused on real-world productivity to receive consecutive invitations. Founder and CEO Jianyu Chen and Co-founder Yue Xi attended the summit . Chen also delivered a keynote speech at APEC Finance Night titled "Putting Robots to Work at Night," sharing ROBOTERA's experience in turning embodied intelligence into practical productivity through real-world logistics deployments.

ROBOTERA has established deployments with China Post and SF Express, with its humanoid robots now operating across over 10 logistics centers. In these real-world operations, the robots achieve parcel induction rates exceeding 1,500 parcels per hour. By taking on repetitive, physically demanding tasks and challenging night shifts, they help address labor shortages while enabling human workers to focus on tasks requiring greater flexibility and judgment.

At the APEC CEO Summit, held from November 17 to 19, ROBOTERA showcased its humanoid robots and logistics solutions, including live parcel sorting demonstrations by its M7 humanoid robot. The demonstration gave international business leaders and attendees a firsthand look at how embodied intelligence is moving beyond technical demonstrations to deliver tangible value in real-world logistics operations.

data.title: European Midday Briefing: Shares Rise as Optimism Improves Ahead of Anthropic Trading Debut
data.description:
MARKET WRAPS

Stocks:

European shares rose as tech sentiment rebounded after Anthropic raised $81 billion in its initial public offering, the biggest of all time.

Anthropic's trading debut will be in focus for the day ahead. "All outward signals suggest a lot of bullishness for the stock, which will be a major barometer of investors' appetite for risk in the AI-trade," said Capital.

Investors will also watch for readouts from the trilateral meeting between President Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen.

Meanwhile, oil prices were mixed as the market weighed expectations of a surplus against continued threats to shipping in the Persian Gulf.

The International Energy Agency said Thursday that prolonged disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz could substantially reduce the world's reliance on the waterway over the next decade as Middle Eastern producers develop alternative export routes.

U.S. Markets:

Stock futures were up as investors expressed optimism over Anthropic's IPO.

Investors were also digesting a hawkish tone struck in minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting.

Forex:

The euro was stable and the currency is consolidating below $1.10 as the strong dollar dominates across the board, ING said.

The dollar eased but stayed near the 19-month high reached overnight after the minutes of the Fed's latest meeting pointed to further interest rate rises. The rising possibility of the Fed increasing interest rates in quick succession at upcoming policy meetings is keeping the dollar strong, MUFG said.

Sterling traded flat. The Bank of England is expected to raise interest rates further to bring U.K. inflation down towards its 2% target and this should support sterling in the near term, Commerzbank said. Bonds:

Eurozone bond yields were slightly higher ahead of heavy bond supply from Spain and France.

Relief in French government bond yield spreads is still possible with the timely passage of a 2027 budget, even if by decree, ING said. Treasury yields turned higher as the minutes of the Fed's October meeting showed readiness to raise interest rates further, potentially at a faster pace.

Energy:

Oil prices were mixed. The IEA expects the global oil market to record a surplus of around 1.7 million barrels a day in the fourth quarter, widening to approximately 3.8 million barrels a day next year as Middle Eastern production recovers faster than demand.

Gas

European natural-gas prices rose in early trading following the previous session's drop, with the benchmark Dutch TTF contract now up 3.7% to 83.80 euros a megawatt hour.

Metals:

Gold prices continued to slip. "Minutes from the October [Federal Open Market Committee] showed strong alignment from Fed officials on the need for additional rate hikes," said MUFG.

Copper

Copper prices remained near their lowest level since April following a broad selloff across commodity markets, driven by a stronger U.S. dollar and growing concerns over AI-related investment.

EMEA HEADLINES

Houthi Attack Damages Saudi Capital's Tallest Tower

DUBAI-A projectile launched by Yemen's Iranian-backed Houthi rebels struck the tallest tower in Saudi Arabia's capital Thursday, causing damage across multiple floors of a building home to the kingdom's sovereign-wealth fund.

The strike on the Public Investment Fund Tower, which stands over Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District, follows a previous Houthi strike on the neighborhood that is home to some of the world's biggest financial firms.

UniCredit Strikes Deal With Germany to Clear Path for Commerzbank Takeover

UniCredit reached an agreement with the German government to resolve key issues in the takeover of Commerzbank, clearing the way for the Italian lender to take control of Germany's second-largest listed bank.

To meet Germany's demands, UniCredit agreed to keep Commerzbank's headquarters in Frankfurt, where the bank will remain listed on the stock exchange, according to a letter from UniCredit Chief Executive Officer Andrea Orcel to German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil.

Deutsche Telekom's Tech Fund Invests $110 Million in Mistral AI

Deutsche Telekom's technology investment fund has invested around $110 million in Mistral AI as part of the French artificial-intelligence startup's Series D funding round.

The AI company completed its latest financing in September, raising a total of 3 billion euros ($3.29 billion) and lifting its valuation above 21 billion euros with backing from existing investors like Samsung Electronics and ASML Holding as well as new investors such as Advent, funds and accounts managed by BlackRock and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.

Novartis Sees Sales Growth Through 2031

Novartis forecast steady sales growth through 2031, citing momentum from drugs already in the market and upcoming launches, and said medicines it has in the pipeline would help it sustain growth over the long term.

The Swiss drugmaker said Thursday that it expects annual sales growth of 5% from 2026 to 2031, excluding the effect of currency movements. It had previously forecast annual sales growth in the 5% to 6% range over the 2025-30 period.

GLOBAL NEWS

Wall Street Pledged to Mobilize $500 Billion for Nvidia-but Hasn't Put Up a Dime

Jensen Huang sensed the winds shifting against Nvidia this spring.

In June, Wall Street giants Apollo Global Management and Blackstone announced a megadeal to help Broadcom, one of Nvidia's main rivals, secure $35 billion of chip financing for Anthropic.

Trump, Xi and Putin Convene First-Ever Summit as World Order Shifts

SHENZHEN, China-President Trump was meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in this southern Chinese city on Thursday, in an unprecedented show of unity among the stewards of the world's three largest nuclear arsenals.

The first-ever gathering of the American, Chinese and Russian leaders is a further sign of the end of a unipolar world order dominated by the U.S.-and suggests that what might replace it is a more uncertain, and unsettled, reality.

Oil Prices Mixed as Traders Weigh Supply Outlook, Middle East Shipping Risks

DOHA, Qatar-Oil prices were mixed Thursday as traders assessed the global supply outlook amid continued threats to Middle Eastern oil shipments and fresh projections for the region's energy trade.

Front-month Brent crude futures rose 0.3% to $92.25 a barrel, while front-month West Texas Intermediate crude futures slipped 0.1% to $83.21 a barrel.

The first-ever gathering of the American, Chinese and Russian leaders is a further sign of the end of a unipolar world order dominated by the U.S.-and suggests that what might replace it is a more uncertain, and unsettled, reality.

Democrats Name Top Targets for Trump Probes

A top House Democrat issued document-preservation notices Wednesday to family members of President Trump and members of his administration, providing an early road map of potential targets of investigations next year.

The demands from Rep. Robert Garcia (D., Calif.), who is set to be the chairman of the Oversight Committee, focus on Trump family business ventures, the Department of Homeland Security's immigration enforcement, White House construction projects and documents related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Insurgents in Iran's Borderlands Are Becoming a Bigger Challenge for the Regime

Heavily armed insurgents in Iran's restive borderlands are posing a new challenge to the embattled leadership in Tehran, carrying out an increasing number of attacks in recent months that have targeted regime security forces.

Militants armed with rocket-propelled grenades and heavy machine guns have ambushed security patrols and attacked intelligence and police buildings in a province along Iran's southeastern border with Pakistan. Militant groups in that region have conducted more than 70 attacks, conflict data monitor Armed Conflict Location and Event Data found, the highest annual number in at least a decade.

Hegseth Cements New Military Deal in Visit to Venezuela

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unexpected visit Wednesday to Caracas, signing a military pact with Venezuela's interim government.

Since the removal of strongman Nicolás Maduro as Venezuela's leader in a U.S. commando operation in January, the two countries have signed oil deals and worked in tandem to strike armed groups inside Venezuelan territory. Hegseth touted the recent cooperation in a formal ceremony with Venezuela's acting president, Delcy Rodríguez, and a phalanx of Venezuelan and American officials.

data.title: CTP Signs New Lease With Airbus at CTPark Brașov
data.description:
CTP Signs New Lease With Airbus at CTPark Brașov

Regulatory News:

CTP, Europe’s largest listed developer, owner and operator of logistics and industrial real estate by gross leasable area (GLA), has signed a new lease with Airbus, a leading aircraft manufacturer, for an 18,000 sqm Build-To-Suit facility at CTPark Brașov in Romania.

Airbus will use the high-quality energy efficient facility at CTPark Brașov for warehousing and logistics activities that enhance its operations. The deal brings one of the world’s most exceptional aerospace companies to CTP’s expanding business park community in Romania. It also marks an important milestone in CTPark Brașov‘s development, demonstrating its attractive strategic position for leading international companies.

Located to the north of Brașov in central Romania's Transylvania region, CTPark Brașov benefits from direct access to the DN13 motorway and is close to the city’s other main infrastructure including Brașov-Ghimbav International Airport. The park is also ideally located for businesses looking to establish or expand their operations in central Romania, with its position in one of the country's most established industrial and manufacturing regions with access to skilled labour, which was an important factor in Airbus’ decision to locate there.

The deal is also testament to the flexibility of CTP’s portfolio and its ability to provide major occupiers such as Airbus with both immediate solutions for space, and solutions for future expansion as needs evolve. With a network of parks across Romania and a portfolio spanning 12 European markets and an extensive landbank, CTP is ready to support clients with Grade A industrial and logistics properties, both in Romania and internationally. This is a key reason why over 70% of new leases CTP signs each year are with existing clients expanding across its network.

Ronald Binkofski, Managing Director, CTP Romania, said:

“We welcome Airbus to CTPark Brașov. One of the world’s most pioneering companies choosing to join CTP’s network demonstrates the quality of our Parks, the properties we deliver, and our capability to understand the needs of modern businesses. This is the latest in a series of leases we have signed with clients in Romania since the start of 2026, with more than 420,000 sqm of leases signed in the first nine months of the year, supported by demand for strategically located industrial and logistics space, continued growth in domestic consumption, and supply chain modernisation.”

Viorela Olteanu, Business Developer, CTP Romania, said:

“Airbus locating at CTPark Brașov is an important milestone for the park and a strong endorsement of Brașov as a location for major international companies. The combination of a high-quality newly delivered building, strong local infrastructure and the industrial park’s strategic position all met Airbus’ requirements, while offering flexibility for future growth both at CTPark Brașov and across CTP’s wider network. The partnerships we have with clients at CTP go far beyond providing space alone. As a developer-landlord that holds its properties for the long term we create the conditions that allow our clients to develop and strategically evolve over time. We look forward to working with Airbus long into the future.”

CTPark Brașov currently comprises approximately 18,000 sqm of built space. There is a further 27,000 sqm of development potential at the park, totaling around 13 hectares for companies seeking space in one of Romania’s key industrial regions.

The agreement with Airbus further strengthens CTP’s position in Romania, one of its largest markets. CTP’s Romanian portfolio comprises more than 3.2 million sqm of logistics and industrial space across key logistics and manufacturing hubs, including in Bucharest, Timișoara, Brașov, Sibiu, Craiova and Arad. Romania accounts for more than 3.2 million sqm of CTP’s 15.1 million sqm European portfolio and remains one of the company’s most important growth markets across Central and Eastern Europe.

About CTP

CTP is Europe’s largest listed developer, owner, and operator of logistics and industrial real estate by gross leasable area ("GLA"), with a portfolio of 15.1 million sqm of GLA in 12 countries and 1.7 million sqm under construction as of 30 September 2026. The company’s ready-built factories and warehouses, together with its custom-built solutions, serve over 1,700 clients ranging from large blue-chip multinationals to local SMEs. CTP builds long-term partnerships through a client-first approach, maintaining roughly 93% annual retention and generating 63% of new business from existing client expansion. All new buildings are certified to the BREEAM standard "Very Good" or higher, underscoring the company’s commitment to sustainable development. CTP holds Investment Grade ratings from S&P: BBB (Stable), Moody’s: Baa2 (Stable), and JCR: A (Stable).

data.title: My wife pays thousands of dollars for her family to visit from Argentina. How can I convince her to stop?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'I don't want my wife to feel that I'm asking her to choose between me and her family'

"Hotel rooms can cost as much as $400 per night, and the total cost of these visits can easily run into several thousand dollars." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

My wife and I have a wonderful marriage, but there is one recurring issue that has become a significant source of frustration for me. While my wife is an exceptionally generous and giving person, I feel that some of her family members have come to take advantage of that generosity.

Several of her relatives regularly want to visit us in New York, traveling from Argentina. Given the long journey, these visits typically last around two weeks. Some of her nieces, nephews and siblings expect to visit virtually every year.

The problem is that we live in a Manhattan apartment with limited space, and hosting guests for extended periods is a significant imposition on our daily routines, privacy and overall quality of life. Now that we also have a baby, the logistical and personal challenges are even greater.

My wife is extremely devoted to her family and, for whatever reason, seems to have difficulty saying no to their requests. I've gently raised my concerns several times, explaining that we simply don't have the space to accommodate so many guests.

Many of her relatives have limited financial means, so my wife often ends up covering not only their flights and accommodations, but also airport transportation, meals, entertainment and other expenses.

Don't miss: My older brother, who has no children, cut our only sister out of his will. I'll get everything instead. Do I tell her?

Space constraints

While I appreciate that this addresses some of the space constraints, it creates a separate issue: the considerable financial burden. Hotel rooms can cost as much as $400 per night, and the total cost of these visits can easily run into several thousand dollars.

Although my wife has her own money, these expenditures still have meaningful opportunity costs for our family. We have substantial financial priorities, including the high cost of childcare in New York City, saving toward purchasing a home and planning for our son's education.

It's also worth noting that we already travel to Argentina every year to visit her family. So it's not as though declining to host relatives in New York would prevent us from maintaining close relationships with them or spending time together.

I love my wife and I genuinely admire her generosity and commitment to her family. However, I'm increasingly feeling that her relatives' expectations are being prioritized over my comfort in our own home, our privacy and our family's financial goals.

I'm concerned that if this continues, my frustration will turn into resentment and undermine what is otherwise an excellent marriage. How can I establish reasonable boundaries? I don't want my wife to feel that I'm asking her to choose between me and her family.

The Husband

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: 'It leaves me with a sour taste': My elderly mother gave our cousin $800 for a car repair. Should I be worried?

She could be afraid of angering or disappointing her relatives, issues that might be rooted in her upbringing and culture.

Dear Husband,

When words fail to change bad habits, enlist a pen and paper.

This is a domestic as well as a financial problem. Your wife is spending money in isolation and without keeping your overall financial goals in mind. You probably are too, perhaps in smaller ways. This bad habit, which only appears to be getting worse, needs to be broken.

The only way to accomplish this is to show her how much money these trips are costing your family, in real terms, as you also pay for childcare and rent, save for emergencies and your child's schooling and college education, and put money aside to buy a home.

Of course, making it personal will only get you both mired in hurt feelings and defensiveness, so you need to take her family out of the equation as much as possible and revisit your marriage vows - your pact to respect and honor each other.

You can have these conversations alone, or with the help of a financial adviser or counselor. I suggest the latter. A mediator can help you articulate your concerns, frame your questions as "I feel ..." rather than "You are ..." and prevent you from hurting each other's feelings.

Ultimately, you need to formulate a family policy rather than take potshots at your wife's family. You have reached a stage in your married life when you are working toward tangible financial goals, and spending thousands of dollars on third parties compromises that.

A financial therapist could help to field your concerns.

Emphasize your shared responsibility and the importance of working as a team. Hosting relatives every year impinges on your privacy and ability to relax in your own home, disrupts your daily routines and makes your responsibilities as new parents more challenging.

Eventually, your wife will have to find the words to say no to people, her family included. It's not always easy, but after you do it once, it gets easier. Given that she has set an unhealthy precedent, this conversation can start with a soft no - and the truth.

She can tell her family: "This year is impossible for us to host. We no longer have room. We have a young child and a lot of family and work commitments." For what it's worth, there's also a difference between relatives visiting your city and crashing at your place.

I feel confident that facing up to the reality of your financial situation will encourage your wife to stop spending money meant for your little family on visiting relatives. Hotels, theater tickets and meals all add up, and something is wrong if her family members all expect the royal treatment.

Any expenditure over $1,000 should have veto power.

Facing that reality means making big decisions together - and spending thousands of dollars a year on visiting relatives is categorically a big decision, even if it seems like it's actually lots of small acts of generosity. Any expenditure over $1,000 should be discussed and agreed upon.

Many couples have a "mutual veto" on a large purchase. Some have a dollar cap, the size of which depends on their income. Unless there are two yes votes, the veto kicks in. But a dollar cap of $1,000 doesn't mean you can spend $999 each on a bunch of relatives.

Finally, many couples have "yours, mine and ours" accounts. They have a joint account for shared bills, savings and vacation money, and smaller personal checking accounts for guilt-free "mad money" splurges. But everything is accounted for in the family ledger.

At the root of this problem is why your wife feels obliged to host her relatives. Our relationship with money is emotional and, although we probably don't like to acknowledge it, less logical than we might imagine. She could be afraid of angering or disappointing her family.

A financial therapist could help explore why your wife feels such a strong sense of familial duty, which may be rooted in her upbringing and culture. She may even feel guilty about having achieved a more financially comfortable life than her relatives.

Whatever the reason behind it, the open-house era of hosting relatives should come to a close.
